issue.title: Incompatible Python version just used (instead of error) when `virtualenvs.create=false`
issue.body:
### Description

When using `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_CREATE="false"` combined with `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_USE_POETRY_PYTHON="true"`, if a project's declared `requires-python` doesn't match the Python used by Poetry, then `poetry sync` won't fail with a "version not compatible error" (as expected), but instead will proceed to sync using the wrong Python version.

This leads to confusing UX for end users of Heroku, if the version specified via their `.python-version` file (which is what controls the Python version installed for their app) doesn't match the Python versions in their `pyproject.toml`.

I believe this is because the conditional here needs additional handling for the value of `create_venv` (which is the value of `virtualenvs.create`):
https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/79c207b41dfb5f9af78fde50d4e5660f7deaf324/src/poetry/utils/env/env_manager.py#L424-L428

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `Dockerfile` with the below contents.
2. `docker build . --progress plain --no-cache`

(Note: I've created this `Dockerfile` as the easiest way to provide a minimal testcase; on Heroku we actually don't use Docker like this and install things in a slightly different way)

```Dockerfile
FROM heroku/heroku:24-build
ARG TARGETARCH
USER root

WORKDIR /testcase

RUN mkdir -p /testcase/.heroku/python \
  && curl -sSf "https://heroku-buildpack-python.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/python-3.13.1-ubuntu-24.04-${TARGETARCH}.tar.zst" \
  | tar -x --zstd -C /testcase/.heroku/python
ENV PATH="/testcase/.heroku/python/bin:${PATH}"
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/testcase/.heroku/python/lib"

RUN which -a python3
RUN /usr/bin/python3 --version
RUN python3 --version

ENV POETRY_HOME="/testcase/.heroku/poetry"
ENV PATH="${POETRY_HOME}/bin:${PATH}"
RUN curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org | python3 - --version 2.1.1

COPY <<EOF pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "testcase-poetry"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = "3.12.*"
dependencies = [
    "typing-extensions"
]
[tool.poetry]
package-mode = false
EOF

COPY <<EOF poetry.lock
[[package]]
name = "typing-extensions"
version = "4.12.2"
description = "Backported and Experimental Type Hints for Python 3.8+"
optional = false
python-versions = ">=3.8"
groups = ["main"]
files = [
    {file = "typing_extensions-4.12.2-py3-none-any.whl", hash = "sha256:04e5ca0351e0f3f85c6853954072df659d0d13fac324d0072316b67d7794700d"},
    {file = "typing_extensions-4.12.2.tar.gz", hash = "sha256:1a7ead55c7e559dd4dee8856e3a88b41225abfe1ce8df57b7c13915fe121ffb8"},
]
[metadata]
lock-version = "2.1"
python-versions = "3.12.*"
content-hash = "30427e182c131408fcdf15a6838a771f7e7c1e67fa6e0c33ccc82194052de8df"
EOF

ENV POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_CREATE="false"
ENV POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_USE_POETRY_PYTHON="true"

RUN poetry install --verbose
RUN python3.13 -c 'import typing_extensions; print(typing_extensions)'
```

## Expected

For `poetry sync` to exit non-zero, with an error message that makes it clear that the Python version is incompatible (since the Poetry Python, which is also the first python on PATH, is 3.13, but yet the `requires-python` lists Python 3.12)  - so end users know they need to fix their project's `requires-python` or else change the Python in the environment.

ie: The `NoCompatiblePythonVersionFoundError` error [here](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/79c207b41dfb5f9af78fde50d4e5660f7deaf324/src/poetry/utils/env/env_manager.py#L424-L428)

## Actual

`poetry sync` outputs:

```
The currently activated Python version 3.13.1 is not supported by the project (3.12.*).
Trying to find and use a compatible version.
Using python3.12 (3.12.3)
```

...where Python 3.12 is actually the distro Python, not the Poetry Python - meaning Poetry has ignored what was configured via `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_USE_POETRY_PYTHON="true"`, and tried to find its own Python instead (which is something we don't want it to do).

In addition, even though Poetry said it was using Python 3.12, it actually goes on to use Poetry Python after all, and so installs the project into a Python 3.13 environment, even though the project isn't compatible with 3.13. As confirmed by the `print(typing_extensions)` step returning:

```
<module 'typing_extensions' from '/testcase/.heroku/python/lib/python3.13/site-packages/typing_extensions.py'>
```

This means the end-user build would appear to succeed, only for the app to potentially crash at run-time when the image is rolled out.

### Workarounds

I couldn't find any.

### Poetry Installation Method

install.python-poetry.org

### Operating System

Debian

### Poetry Version

2.1.1

### Poetry Configuration

```bash session
POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_CREATE="false"
POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_USE_POETRY_PYTHON="true"
```

issue.title: Experimental pipeline: `Interval` bounds of zero are silently dropped
issue.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

In `pydantic/experimental/pipeline.py`, `_apply_constraint()` handles `annotated_types.Interval` by delegating to the individual comparison constraints, but it tests each bound for **truthiness** rather than `is not None`:

```python
elif isinstance(constraint, annotated_types.Interval):
    if constraint.ge:
        s = _apply_constraint(s, annotated_types.Ge(constraint.ge))
    if constraint.gt:
        s = _apply_constraint(s, annotated_types.Gt(constraint.gt))
    if constraint.le:
        s = _apply_constraint(s, annotated_types.Le(constraint.le))
    if constraint.lt:
        s = _apply_constraint(s, annotated_types.Lt(constraint.lt))
```

Since `0` is falsy, **a bound of exactly zero is skipped and the constraint is silently dropped** - there is no error, validation simply accepts out-of-range values. `Interval(ge=0, le=10)` happily accepts `-5`.

All four bounds are affected. Observed on 2.12.5:

| constraint | input | expected | actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Interval(ge=0, le=10)` | `-5` | ValidationError | **accepted** |
| `Interval(ge=0, le=10)` | `20` | ValidationError | ValidationError (`le=10` works) |
| `Interval(gt=0)` | `-5` | ValidationError | **accepted** |
| `Interval(gt=0)` | `0` | ValidationError | **accepted** |
| `Interval(le=0)` | `5` | ValidationError | **accepted** |
| `Interval(lt=0)` | `5` | ValidationError | **accepted** |
| `Interval(ge=1, le=10)` | `-5` | ValidationError | ValidationError (control: non-zero bound is fine) |

The non-zero control confirms the trigger is specifically the zero bound, not `Interval` in general. Zero is a very common lower bound, so this silently weakens validation in ordinary usage.

The fix looks like changing the four checks to `if constraint.ge is not None:` (and likewise for `gt`/`le`/`lt`).

This is related to, but distinct from, #13446 - that one is about `Gt` being dropped on a numeric type mismatch, whereas this is the `Interval` branch dropping zero bounds regardless of type.

Happy to open a PR if that would help.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated

import annotated_types
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic.experimental.pipeline import validate_as

ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).constrain(annotated_types.Interval(ge=0, le=10))])

print(ta.validate_python(-5))  # -> -5   (expected: ValidationError, ge=0 is violated)
ta.validate_python(20)         # -> ValidationError (le=10 is enforced correctly)

# A non-zero lower bound behaves correctly:
ta2 = TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).constrain(annotated_types.Interval(ge=1, le=10))])
ta2.validate_python(-5)        # -> ValidationError (correct)
```

issue.title: poetry install skips valid files when a package's lock entry mixes sha256 and sha512 (JSON index)
issue.body:
### Description

## Summary

When a package index's JSON simple API (PEP 691) lists several hashes for a file, and the package's lock entry contains hashes of more than one algorithm, `poetry install` rejects files even though one of their listed hashes exactly matches the hash locked for that file.

The rejected files are skipped with only a debug log line. If the sdist still matches, Poetry silently builds from source instead of using the wheel. Once no installable file is left, the install fails with;

- 2.4.x: `Unable to find installation candidates for markupsafe (3.0.0)` /
  `59 wheel(s) were skipped as your project's environment does not support the identified abi tags`

- 2.5.x: `Downloaded distributions for markupsafe (3.0.0) did not match any known checksums in your lock file.`

I believe that this bug has been present from `2.3.0` and above, when Poetry was changed to prefer JSON over HTML indexes for legacy and private repositories. The error differs between versions, but the underlying cause is the same.

If any of the distributions for the desired version of a package present a `sha512` hash, this will then be selected from the JSON index hash array to match against the lockfile, and the `sha256` hash will be discarded. As a result of this, packages that are presenting a valid `sha256` hash from the JSON index are then ignored, despite the hash presented matching the hash in the lockfile.

## Context

We are consuming packages from a local PyPI mirror using a product called ProGet (built by Inedo) - ProGet is configured in our environment to use lazy caching, where we are mirroring pypi.org public packages, but only caching a specific distribution locally after the first install. 

This bug has to light due to the way ProGet handles algorithms for cached vs uncached packages, where the JSON index will present a `sha256` hash only for uncached packages (which will make its way into the poetry lockfile if this is the first timing consuming a new distribution), and an array of hashes (sha256, sha512, md1, md5) for distributions that have been cached. 

A similar bug was present (and fixed) in `uv`, 
https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/17143

Whilst we agree that presenting a different set of hashes for cached vs uncached packages via the JSON index is peculiar behaviour on the ProGet side, it does still conform with PEP 691, as there is nothing in the spec against this. 

This is mostly an interoperability issue between the two products, but I believe the core bug here is that Poetry makes an assumption that the PEP spec does not guarantee - that the type of hashing algorithms presented in the JSON index will not change between lock and install of packages.

### Workarounds

Re-running a `poetry lock` will modify the failed package in the lockfile from a `sha256` hash to a `sha512` hash, which will resolve the issue until pumping.

issue.title: CORS: the middleware misclassifies all OPTIONS requests as preflight requests
issue.body:
### Issue Description

Echo's CORS middleware misclassifies all `OPTIONS` requests as preflight requests, thereby unduly preventing requests from hitting user-registered `OPTIONS` endpoints.

I've previously discussed the general problem on [my personal blog](https://jub0bs.com/posts/2023-02-08-fearless-cors/#4-categorise-requests-correctly) and how Echo suffers from it in issue #2510.

### Checklist

- [x] Dependencies installed
- [x] No typos
- [x] Searched existing issues and docs

### Expected behaviour

(For this section and the next, please refer to the server code below.)

Consider the `OPTIONS` requests resulting from the following two `curl` commands:

```shell
curl -v -XOPTIONS \
  localhost:8080/hello
```
```shell
curl -v -XOPTIONS \
  -H "Origin: https://example.com" \
  localhost:8080/hello
```

According to [the Fetch standard](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#cors-preflight-request), neither request is a preflight request, because
- the first one lacks both an `Origin` header and an `Access-Control-Request-Method` header, and
- the second one lacks an `Access-Control-Request-Method` header.

Therefore, those requests should get through the CORS middleware, exercise the handler registered on `/hello`, and get a response of this kind:

```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Allow: GET, OPTIONS
Date: Mon, 23 Oct 2023 12:30:33 GMT
```

In contrast, an `OPTIONS` requests resulting from the following `curl` command is a bona fide preflight request; as such, it should be (and is) intercepted and handled by the CORS middleware:

```shell
curl -v -XOPTIONS \
  -H "Origin: https://example.com" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: PUT" \
  localhost:8080/hello
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: PUT
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Vary: Origin
Vary: Access-Control-Request-Method
Vary: Access-Control-Request-Headers
-snip-
```

### Actual behaviour

The first two aforementioned `OPTIONS` requests get intercepted and handled by the CORS middleware rather than by the handler registered on `OPTIONS /hello`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the program to start the server.
2. Exercise it via `curl`(see commands above).

### Working code to debug

```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v4"
	"github.com/labstack/echo/v4/middleware"
)

func main() {
	e := echo.New()
	e.Use(middleware.CORSWithConfig(middleware.CORSConfig{
		AllowOrigins: []string{"*"},
		AllowMethods: []string{http.MethodPut},
	}))
	e.GET("/hello", func(c echo.Context) error {
		return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Hello, World!")
	})
	e.OPTIONS("/hello", func(c echo.Context) error {
		c.Response().Header().Set("Allow", "GET, OPTIONS")
		c.Response().WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
		return nil
	})
	if err := e.Start(":8080"); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
		e.Logger.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

### Version/commit

Echo v4.11.2. See my `go.mod` below:

```
module whatever

go 1.21.3

require github.com/labstack/echo/v4 v4.11.2

require (
	github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v3.2.2+incompatible // indirect
```

issue.title: robots.txt enforcement fails OPEN for 2nd+ concurrent same-host request (RobotsTxtMiddleware + Twisted Deferred.asFuture())
issue.body:
## What happened

With `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, a path disallowed by robots.txt was fetched (HTTP 200) instead of being blocked — but only when it was the **2nd or later concurrent request to the same host**. Reproduced 4/4 runs, deterministically.

**Versions:** Scrapy 2.19, Python 3.12 (Twisted as bundled with the Scrapy 2.19 install — exact version available on request).

## Reproduction

1. Serve a local test site (`python -m http.server`) with robots.txt containing:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /private/
```
2. Run a spider with `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, `DOWNLOAD_DELAY=1.0`, `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN=1`, AutoThrottle enabled, honest User-Agent, requesting three URLs on that host: a live page, a 404, and `/private/x.html`.
3. Observe: `/private/x.html` returns 200 and reaches the parse callback instead of being filtered by the robots middleware.

## Root cause (instrumented)

Concurrent same-host requests share a single Twisted `Deferred` for the robots.txt fetch/parse inside `RobotsTxtMiddleware`. The middleware converts that Deferred per-waiter via `Deferred.asFuture()` — and Twisted's `asFuture()` delivers the real result to the **first** future and **`None`** to the second. The second waiter therefore gets `parser=None`, and `process_request_2` treats `None` as "no parser available → allow the request."

So robots.txt enforcement **silently fails open** for every concurrent same-host request after the first, on the very first robots.txt fetch for a host.

## Expected behavior

All waiters on the shared robots.txt Deferred should receive the parsed result (or all should fail closed — block the request — if the parse result is unavailable).

## Suggested fix directions

- Share the *parsed* result (not the raw Deferred) across waiters; or
- Fail closed: treat `parser=None` as "deny" rather than "allow" in `process_request_2`.

## Workaround

Serialize same-host requests so two requests never race the first robots.txt fetch of a host (e.g. `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN=1` plus a per-host delay), or pre-fetch robots.txt before crawling.

## Why this matters

Fail-open robots.txt enforcement is a compliance footgun: users who set `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True` believe disallowed paths are never fetched. Under concurrency, that guarantee silently breaks.

---
*Found while building a polite liveness-checker that deliberately serializes per-host requests; the serialization accidentally immunized us, which is how the race was isolated. Happy to provide the minimal spider + test server scripts.*

### Issue Description

Given a file on disk with a percent sign in its name, it is not possible to download it using echo's static middleware.

Given some file names:
- `100%.txt`
- `foo%20bar.txt` (this is really the name on disk)

It is not possible to download these files using the static middleware.

### Checklist

- [X] Dependencies installed
- [X] No typos
- [X] Searched existing issues and docs

### Expected behaviour

The standard way to download them would be using the folowing paths:

- `100%.txt` -> `GET /100%25.txt`
- `foo%20bar.txt` -> `GET /foo%2520bar.txt`


### Actual behaviour

- `100%.txt` -> `GET /100%25.txt`
  - echo error message: **`invalid URL escape "%.p`** (because of the double unescape and `.p` is no valid hex)
- `foo%20bar.txt` -> `GET /foo%2520bar.txt`
  - echo error message: **`path does not exist`** (because file `foo bar.txt` does not exist, only `foo%20bar.txt`)

Background is that url.Path in http.Request is already escaped (as the documentation for url.Path suggests), but echo is unescaping it again.

I tried to generate a fix. For the non-embedded case this is solved by simply removing the explicit url.PathUnescape call in static.go (see https://github.com/georgmu/echo/commit/852dedeca2a22a0b6967e71f69cbb0823959a198 which also contains some test cases). I haven't created a merge request yet, as the embedding using groups or path patterns is a bit more complicated (I haven't fully understand the case for the disablePathUnescaping toggle).

### Steps to reproduce / Working code to debug

See test cases in https://github.com/georgmu/echo/commit/852dedeca2a22a0b6967e71f69cbb0823959a198

issue.title: Incorrect Pydantic dataclass constructor signature when using `kw_only=True` in decorator and `pydantic.Field(kw_only=False)`
issue.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Example Code

```Python
import dataclasses
import inspect

import pydantic


@dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
class NormalDataclass:
    a: int = dataclasses.field(kw_only=False)


@pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
class PydanticDataclassWithDataclassField:
    a: int = dataclasses.field(kw_only=False)


@pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
class PydanticDataclassWithPydanticField:
    a: int = pydantic.Field(kw_only=False) # This should show in the signature as not being keyword-only.


for cls in [
    NormalDataclass,
    PydanticDataclassWithDataclassField,
    PydanticDataclassWithPydanticField,
]:
    instance = cls(1)  # Runs fine, type-checks fine.
    assert instance.a == 1
    print(f"{cls.__name__}: {inspect.signature(cls)}")
```

### Description

The example code above prints:

```
NormalDataclass: (a: int) -> None
PydanticDataclassWithDataclassField: (a: int) -> None
PydanticDataclassWithPydanticField: (*, a: int = <factory>) -> None
```

When I would have expected all the signatures to be the same:

```
NormalDataclass: (a: int) -> None
PydanticDataclassWithDataclassField: (a: int) -> None
PydanticDataclassWithPydanticField: (a: int) -> None
```

All of these classes still accept passing a positional argument for `a` to the constructor, but the signature for `PydanticDataclassWithPydanticField` is wrong, incorrectly showing `a` as a keyword-only argument, as well as showing a default value when the argument is actually required.

This appears to be an issue here at `pydantic._internal._dataclasses`:

```python
def as_dataclass_field(pydantic_field: FieldInfo) -> dataclasses.Field[Any]:
    field_args: dict[str, Any] = {'default': pydantic_field}

    # Needed because if `doc` is set, the dataclass slots will be a dict (field name -> doc) instead of a tuple:
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 14) and pydantic_field.description is not None:
        field_args['doc'] = pydantic_field.description

    # Needed as the stdlib dataclass module processes kw_only in a specific way during class construction:
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 10) and pydantic_field.kw_only:
        field_args['kw_only'] = True

    # Needed as the stdlib dataclass modules generates `__repr__()` during class construction:
    if pydantic_field.repr is not True:
        field_args['repr'] = pydantic_field.repr

    return dataclasses.field(**field_args)
```

If I modify the `kw_only` section to always assign the Pydantic field's `kw_only` to the dataclass field when set, the example code will correctly show `a` can be passed as a keyword argument:

```python
    # Needed as the stdlib dataclass module processes kw_only in a specific way during class construction:
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 10) and pydantic_field.kw_only is not None:
        field_args['kw_only'] = pydantic_field.kw_only
```

And the example output will then show:

```
PydanticDataclassWithPydanticField: (a: int = <factory>) -> None
```

There's still the <factory> default, which I'm not sure how to handle.

### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] This is NOT a [security, `npm audit`, or GitHub Advisory issue](https://mochajs.org/explainers/security-vulnerability-reports).
- [x] I have read and agree to Mocha's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)

- [x] I have 'smoke tested' the code to be tested by running it outside the real test suite to get a better sense of whether the problem is in the code under test, my usage of Mocha, or Mocha itself.
- [x] I want to provide a PR to resolve this

### Expected

`mocha --list-reporters` lists the built-in reporters with their descriptions like it does on 11.x.

### Actual

It prints two blank lines and exits 0.

### Minimal, Complete and Verifiable Example

lists 13 reporters:
```sh
npx mocha@11.8.0 --list-reporters
```

prints nothing:
```sh
npx mocha@12.0.2 --list-reporters
```

### Versions

mocha 12.0.2 (also on main), node v24.17.0, Windows 11.

### Additional Info

Reporters switched to ES2015 classes in #5180. Unlike `util.inherits`, `class extends` inherits statics so `Base.abstract = true` is inherited by every reporter and the listing skips them all.

The test uses the same flag to build its expected list and therfore producing an empty array and asserting nothing so it stayed green.
